name: Card Transaction Authorisation
triggering_persona_note: PER-009 is an external system actor, not a human. The card network forwards an ISO 8583 or ISO 20022 authorisation request on behalf of the cardholder (PER-001) when the cardholder presents their debit or credit card at a point of sale, ATM, or e-commerce checkout.
orchestration_notes: Card Transaction Authorisation is a CHANNEL interaction. PER-009 (the card network) is the external caller of the Card Processing API (SVC-011). SVC-011 makes the authorisation decision using its OWN local data: cached balance, pre-loaded fraud rules, card status, and 3DS result. It does NOT call other capabilities synchronously — the <500ms Visa/Mastercard latency SLA makes synchronous cross-capability calls architecturally impermissible. Post-authorisation, SVC-011 publishes events that are consumed asynchronously by SVC-013 (fraud pattern learning) and SVC-001/SVC-003 (balance reservation). This is a high-throughput, real-time journey with strict latency requirements distinct from all other bank journeys.
sca_method: 3DS 2.x (EMV 3-D Secure) for card-not-present transactions. Chip-and-PIN (EMV) for card-present transactions. Contactless exemption applies for transactions below £100 (UK FCA SCA exemption) and for cumulative contactless limit enforcement.

latency_constraint.rationale: Visa and Mastercard authorisation network SLAs require an authorisation response within 500ms of the request arriving at the issuer. Failure to respond within the window results in a network timeout, which is treated as a decline by the acquirer. This constraint prohibits any synchronous cross-capability API call during the authorisation decision path.
latency_constraint.visa_rule_reference: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, Section 1 (Transaction Processing)
latency_constraint.mastercard_rule_reference: Mastercard Transaction Processing Rules, Chapter 2 (Transaction Processing Requirements)

phases.name: Authorisation Request
phases.description: The card network (PER-009) sends an authorisation request to SVC-011 via the bank's card scheme connectivity. The request conforms to ISO 8583 or ISO 20022 card scheme message standards and contains the card token, merchant ID, merchant name, transaction amount, currency, and (for CNP transactions) the 3DS 2.x authentication result. SVC-011 receives the request via the card scheme host gateway and begins the real-time decision process.
channel: Card Scheme Network (Visa / Mastercard) — ISO 8583 or ISO 20022 message
persona_actions: PER-009 (Card Network): Forwards ISO 8583 / ISO 20022 authorisation request from the acquiring bank to the issuing bank (SVC-011) via the card scheme network
PER-001 (Cardholder): Has presented their debit or credit card at the merchant terminal — no further action required during authorisation
system_actions: Card scheme network routes the authorisation request to SVC-011 based on the BIN (Bank Identification Number)
SVC-011 receives the request on the card scheme host gateway
SVC-011 tokenises the PAN to card_number_token if not already tokenised; the raw PAN never exits the PCI CDE
SVC-011 looks up the CardAuthorisation record by card_number_token to hydrate account context
SVC-011 publishes CardAuthorisationRequested (EVT-064) to the event bus for audit trail
entry_conditions: Valid ISO 8583 or ISO 20022 authorisation request received from card network
exit_conditions: CardAuthorisation entity created with status = pending_decision; EVT-064 published

phases.name: Real-Time Decision
phases.description: SVC-011 makes the authorisation decision using local data only — no synchronous cross-capability calls. Decision inputs: (1) card status check from local card status cache; (2) balance/limit check from local pre-cached balance (debit: account.available_balance; credit: card_account.available_balance); (3) pre-loaded fraud rule evaluation (velocity rules, geography rules, MCC restrictions, daily limits) using SVC-011's local rule engine; (4) 3DS 2.x authentication result for CNP transactions (result embedded in the authorisation request). SVC-011 must produce an authorisation decision within the card network latency budget.
channel: Internal — SVC-011 local decision engine; no customer-facing interaction
persona_actions: PER-001 (Cardholder): Waiting at the merchant terminal for authorisation approval. No action required.
Card Network (PER-009): Awaiting the authorisation response from SVC-011
system_actions: SVC-011 checks card status (active/suspended/blocked) from local cache — decline if not active
SVC-011 checks balance: debit card → Account.available_balance from local cache; credit card → CreditCardAccount.available_balance from local cache. Decline if insufficient

SVC-011 evaluates pre-loaded fraud rules: velocity (transactions per hour), geography (country of use vs cardholder home country), MCC category restrictions, daily spend limits. Decline or refer if rules triggered
SVC-011 checks 3DS 2.x result for CNP transactions: authenticated (proceed), attempted (accept with increased chargeback liability), not authenticated (decline)
SVC-011 applies SCA exemption logic: contactless < £100 (FCA SCA RTS Article 11), recurring transaction exemption (FCA SCA RTS Article 14), TRA exemption for low-value CNP (FCA SCA RTS Article 18)
SVC-011 derives authorisation decision: approved | declined | referred
SVC-011 generates authorisation code (6-character alphanumeric) for approved transactions
SVC-011 records processing_time_ms on the CardAuthorisation entity
entry_conditions: CardAuthorisation entity created with status = pending_decision
exit_conditions: CardAuthorisation.status updated to approved | declined | referred; decision logged locally before response sent
nfr_references: NFR-JRN011-001 — total decision time contributes to sub-500ms response target

phases.name: Authorisation Response
phases.description: SVC-011 sends the authorisation response back to the card network (PER-009) via the card scheme host gateway. The response contains the authorisation code (if approved) or decline reason code (if declined). The card network forwards the response to the acquirer, which relays it to the merchant terminal. The cardholder sees the result (approved/declined) on the merchant terminal within approximately 2-4 seconds of tapping/inserting their card.
channel: Card Scheme Network (Visa / Mastercard) — ISO 8583 or ISO 20022 response message
persona_actions: PER-001 (Cardholder): Views authorisation result on merchant terminal (APPROVED or DECLINED)
PER-009 (Card Network): Receives authorisation response and forwards to acquirer
system_actions: SVC-011 formats ISO 8583 / ISO 20022 authorisation response with action code (approved: 00; declined: scheme-standard reason code)
SVC-011 transmits response to card scheme host gateway
Card network routes response to acquiring bank → merchant terminal
SVC-011 publishes CardAuthorisationCompleted (EVT-065) for approved transactions
SVC-011 publishes CardAuthorisationDeclined (EVT-066) for declined transactions
NO raw PAN is included in any event payload — card_number_token is used exclusively
exit_conditions: Authorisation response sent to card network; EVT-065 (approved) or EVT-066 (declined) published
governance_references: PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3.5 — no PAN in event payloads
nfr_references: NFR-JRN011-001 — response must reach card network within 500ms of request receipt

phases.name: Post-Authorisation Processing
phases.description: After the authorisation response is sent, SVC-011 publishes events for downstream async consumers. SVC-013 (Fraud Detection / CAP-004) consumes CardAuthorisationCompleted asynchronously for fraud pattern learning and behavioural model training — not for real-time blocking. SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core / CAP-001) or SVC-003 (Credit Card Service / CAP-001) consumes CardAuthorisationCompleted to apply a balance reservation (soft block) against the account, reflecting the pending authorisation. If suspicious activity is detected in the post-auth analysis, SVC-013 may publish SuspiciousCardActivityDetected (EVT-068) to initiate a fraud case.
channel: Internal async — event bus (SVC-102). No customer-facing interaction.
persona_actions: PER-001 (Cardholder): No action required. Balance reservation will be visible in their account balance view.
PER-054 (Fraud Analyst): May receive alert if SuspiciousCardActivityDetected (EVT-068) is published
system_actions: SVC-013 consumes CardAuthorisationCompleted (EVT-065): updates real-time transaction velocity counters, enriches cardholder behaviour model, evaluates post-auth fraud patterns
SVC-013 publishes SuspiciousCardActivityDetected (EVT-068) if post-auth pattern analysis identifies suspicious activity — this creates a fraud case for PER-054 investigation

SVC-001 (debit cards) or SVC-003 (credit cards) consumes CardAuthorisationCompleted (EVT-065): applies balance reservation by debiting available_balance by the authorised amount. Reservation is pending until settlement (PH-045)
SVC-103 (Audit & Logging) consumes all card authorisation events for immutable WORM audit trail (PCI DSS v4.0 Req 10.2, card scheme dispute evidence)
entry_conditions: EVT-065 (CardAuthorisationCompleted) or EVT-066 (CardAuthorisationDeclined) published by SVC-011
exit_conditions: Balance reservation applied on account; fraud model updated; audit log written
nfr_references: NFR-JRN011-004 — balance reservation applied within 2 seconds of EVT-065 publication

phases.name: Clearing and Settlement
phases.description: At end of day, the acquiring bank submits clearing files to the card scheme. SVC-011 receives the clearing data, matches each clearing item to its pre-authorisation record (ENT-032), and initiates settlement. Settlement amounts may differ from the authorisation amount (e.g. tip added, currency conversion variance). SVC-011 creates the CardSettlement entity (ENT-033) recording the final settled amount, interchange fee, and scheme fee. SVC-001 or SVC-003 consumes CardSettlementProcessed (EVT-067) to post the final debit to the account ledger and release the balance reservation.
channel: Card scheme clearing file (batch) — end of day processing
persona_actions: PER-001 (Cardholder): No action required. Settled transaction will appear as a confirmed debit in their statement.
Payment Operations Team (PER-040): Monitors settlement reconciliation; investigates any unmatched clearing items
system_actions: SVC-011 receives end-of-day clearing file from card scheme network
SVC-011 matches each clearing item to the pre-authorised ENT-032 (CardAuthorisation) by auth_id
SVC-011 creates ENT-033 (CardSettlement) with final settlement_amount, interchange_fee, scheme_fee, net_amount
SVC-011 publishes CardSettlementProcessed (EVT-067)
SVC-001 (debit) or SVC-003 (credit) consumes EVT-067: posts final debit to account ledger; releases balance reservation created in PH-044; updates account.available_balance to reflect settled amount
SVC-011 calls SVC-009 (Domestic Payments, same-capability) for settlement funds movement via BACS/CHAPS as required
SVC-103 writes settlement records to WORM audit pipeline (7-year retention for Visa/Mastercard dispute resolution and FCA BCOBS)
entry_conditions: Clearing file received from card scheme; matching pre-authorised CardAuthorisation records exist in ENT-032
exit_conditions: ENT-033 (CardSettlement) created; EVT-067 published; final ledger debit posted by SVC-001/SVC-003
governance_references: FCA BCOBS — account transaction records 7 years
nfr_references: NFR-JRN011-005 — settlement processing completed by 06:00 on T+1

happy_path.description: Cardholder (PER-001) presents their active debit or credit card at a merchant terminal. Card network (PER-009) routes the ISO 8583 authorisation request to SVC-011. SVC-011 checks card status (active), verifies sufficient balance in local cache, evaluates pre-loaded fraud rules (all clear), checks 3DS result for CNP (authenticated). Decision: APPROVED. Authorisation code generated. Response returned to card network within 500ms. EVT-065 published. Balance reservation applied asynchronously by SVC-001/SVC-003. Fraud model updated asynchronously by SVC-013. End of day: clearing file received, CardSettlement created, EVT-067 published, final ledger debit posted.

timing_breakdown.clearing_and_settlement_batch: End of day (T+0 clearing → T+1 settlement)

alternative_paths.name: 3DS 2.x Challenge Required (CNP Transaction)
alternative_paths.description: For card-not-present (e-commerce) transactions where TRA exemption does not apply or the fraud risk score warrants a challenge, SVC-011 may trigger a 3DS 2.x challenge flow. The ACS (Access Control Server) — co-located within SVC-011's PCI CDE — presents a challenge to the cardholder (biometric, OTP, or knowledge-based). The authorisation request is held pending the 3DS result. On successful authentication, the authorisation proceeds. Challenge adds 20-30 seconds to the CNP transaction but is outside the 500ms card network timeout window (the 3DS challenge occurs before the ISO 8583 authorisation request is sent by the acquirer).
alternative_paths.diverges_at: PH-041 (before ISO 8583 request received — 3DS challenge completes at acquirer before auth request sent)
alternative_paths.sca_exemptions_not_applicable: Transaction amount above TRA threshold or cardholder risk profile elevated

alternative_paths.name: SCA Contactless Exemption
alternative_paths.description: For contactless debit and credit card transactions below £100 (FCA SCA RTS Article 11 low-value payment exemption), SVC-011 applies the contactless exemption during PH-042 fraud rule evaluation. No 3DS challenge required. Cumulative contactless limit tracking (5 consecutive contactless transactions or cumulative total above £300 since last SCA) is enforced by the local rule engine. When the cumulative limit is reached, SVC-011 flags the next transaction for SCA enforcement (customer must insert card and enter PIN).
alternative_paths.diverges_at: PH-042 (SCA exemption applied — no 3DS check required)
alternative_paths.cumulative_limit_tracking: SVC-011 maintains cumulative_contactless_amount and contactless_transaction_count in local card state cache. Resets on each SCA-authenticated transaction.

alternative_paths.name: Referred Transaction — Manual Review
alternative_paths.description: Some authorisation requests produce a 'referred' decision from the automated rule engine — typically because the transaction triggers a review rule (not an outright block) and the rule engine cannot confirm approval without human judgement. The card network receives a referral response code. In some card-present scenarios, the merchant may be prompted to call the bank's authorisation centre. A Payment Operations agent (PER-040) reviews the transaction and can approve or decline. This path is rare in modern card processing — most referrals are resolved by the automated engine.
alternative_paths.volume_note: < 0.1% of authorisation requests result in a referral. Most are resolved within 60 seconds.

exception_paths.name: Insufficient Balance (Debit Card)
exception_paths.description: SVC-011 checks the local balance cache during PH-042 and determines the account's available_balance is insufficient to cover the transaction amount. Decision: DECLINED. Decline reason code D51 (insufficient funds) returned to card network. CardAuthorisationDeclined (EVT-066) published with decline_reason = insufficient_funds. No balance information is disclosed in the event payload beyond what is required for async downstream consumers.
exception_paths.customer_experience: Merchant terminal shows DECLINED. Customer must use alternative payment method.

exception_paths.name: Credit Limit Exceeded (Credit Card)
exception_paths.description: SVC-011 checks the local balance cache during PH-042 and determines the CreditCardAccount's available_balance (credit_limit minus current outstanding) is insufficient. Decision: DECLINED. Decline reason code D51 returned.
governance_references: FCA CONC 6.7 — responsible lending; credit limit may not be exceeded

exception_paths.name: Card Blocked or Suspended
exception_paths.description: SVC-011 checks local card status cache during PH-042. Card status = blocked (reported lost/stolen) or suspended (account suspended by bank). Decision: DECLINED. Decline reason code D41 (lost card) or D43 (stolen card) or D62 (restricted card) returned as appropriate.
governance_references: PSD2/PSRs 2017 — card issuer obligations on lost/stolen card response time

exception_paths.name: Fraud Rule Block (Pre-loaded Rule)
exception_paths.description: SVC-011's local fraud rule engine triggers a block during PH-042 — e.g. transaction velocity exceeded, geographic anomaly (card used abroad without travel notification), MCC restriction (gambling merchant blocked by default), or single transaction limit exceeded. Decision: DECLINED. CardAuthorisationDeclined (EVT-066) published with decline_reason = fraud_rule_triggered. SVC-013 is notified asynchronously via EVT-066 consumption to update velocity counters and flag for post-auth pattern review.
exception_paths.trigger: Local fraud rule evaluation returns block outcome in PH-042
exception_paths.card_network_response_code: D05 (Do Not Honour) or D57 (Transaction Not Permitted) depending on rule type
governance_references: PSR PS23/3 — fraud prevention; FCA Consumer Duty — customer must be informed of spending controls

exception_paths.name: Suspicious Activity Detected Post-Authorisation
exception_paths.description: SVC-013 consumes CardAuthorisationCompleted (EVT-065) in PH-044 and, during async post-auth pattern analysis, identifies that the authorised transaction is part of a suspicious pattern (e.g. the card has been used in 3 geographically impossible locations within 10 minutes — not detectable pre-auth from a single transaction but visible in post-auth aggregation). SVC-013 publishes SuspiciousCardActivityDetected (EVT-068). This triggers a fraud case creation and may trigger a card block request back to SVC-011 to prevent further transactions. The originally approved transaction is already settled — no reversal from this exception path alone.
exception_paths.trigger: SVC-013 post-auth pattern analysis detects suspicious activity on card_number_token after EVT-065 consumed
exception_paths.consequence: Fraud case created; PER-054 (Fraud Analyst) alerted; card may be suspended pending investigation; customer notified per FCA Consumer Duty
governance_references: PSR PS23/3 — fraud detection obligation; PCI DSS v4.0 Req 10.2

exception_paths.name: Balance Cache Staleness — Fallback Decision
exception_paths.description: If SVC-011's local balance cache is stale (last refresh > 30 seconds ago) and cannot be immediately refreshed within the authorisation latency budget, SVC-011 applies a conservative fallback: (a) for debit cards with a cached balance above the transaction amount plus a 10% buffer, approve the transaction (accepting the risk of a small overdraft); (b) for debit cards where the cached balance is below the amount or within the buffer, decline. This fallback behaviour is governed by a configurable staleness policy and is designed to avoid systematic false declines during brief cache refresh outages.
exception_paths.trigger: Cache age > 30 seconds for the specific card at the time of the authorisation request
exception_paths.fallback_policy: Approve if cached_balance > transaction_amount * 1.10; decline otherwise
governance_references: Visa/Mastercard scheme rules on stand-in processing

design_decisions.decision: SVC-011 (Card Processing) makes the authorisation decision using LOCAL data only — no synchronous cross-capability API calls during the authorisation path.
design_decisions.rationale: Visa and Mastercard authorisation network SLAs mandate a response within 500ms. The bank's event-driven architecture principle permits synchronous API calls only within the same capability. SVC-011 (CAP-003.05) cannot synchronously call SVC-001 (CAP-001) or SVC-013 (CAP-004) without violating both the latency constraint and the cross-capability API prohibition. Resolution: pre-load the authorisation decision inputs (balance cache, card status, fraud rules) from a local high-performance cache maintained by SVC-011. The cache is kept warm via async events consumed from SVC-001/SVC-003 (balance updates) and SVC-013 (fraud rule updates).
alternatives_considered: Synchronous cross-capability call to SVC-001/SVC-003 for live balance at authorisation time
Synchronous call to SVC-013 for live fraud scoring at authorisation time
design_decisions.rejected_because: Both alternatives violate the 500ms card network latency SLA and the bank's cross-capability async-only architectural principle. Network round-trip to SVC-001 or SVC-013 (even within the same data centre) would add 10-50ms plus processing time — acceptable for FPS (15-second budget) but not for card authorisation (500ms total budget including card scheme network transit).

design_decisions.decision: PCI DSS scope: SVC-011 operates as the PCI CDE boundary. card_number_token (format-preserving token from the tokenisation vault) is the only card identifier used in all events, APIs, and entity fields outside the PCI CDE. Raw PAN is never stored in SVC-001, SVC-003, or any event payload.
design_decisions.rationale: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 3.5 prohibits storage of PAN in clear text outside the PCI CDE. Using card_number_token as the universal card identifier limits PCI CDE scope to SVC-011 and its HSM-backed tokenisation vault, materially reducing the certification boundary and audit cost. ENT-023 (CreditCardAccount) and ENT-032 (CardAuthorisation) both use card_number_token exclusively.
design_decisions.pci_scope_note: SVC-011 is PCI DSS scoped (Tier T3, CAP-003). SVC-001, SVC-003, SVC-013, and all event bus topics are out of PCI CDE scope.

design_decisions.decision: Post-authorisation cross-capability coordination is exclusively async events via SVC-102. SVC-013 and SVC-001/SVC-003 consume CardAuthorisationCompleted asynchronously — they do not need to complete before the authorisation response is returned to the card network.
design_decisions.rationale: Balance reservation and fraud model updates are non-blocking post-conditions — they do not affect the authorisation decision already made. The card network only waits for the authorisation response (PH-043), not for downstream balance or fraud model state changes. Async event consumption ensures the authorisation decision path remains unencumbered by downstream processing latency.
design_decisions.implementation_note: At-least-once delivery semantics apply to EVT-065 and EVT-066. SVC-001/SVC-003 and SVC-013 must be idempotent consumers keyed on auth_id.

design_decisions.decision: Balance reservation is a soft block applied asynchronously (PH-044). The hard ledger debit is applied only at clearing/settlement (PH-045).
design_decisions.rationale: This is consistent with the four-party card scheme settlement model: authorisation creates a reservation; clearing delivers the final amount; settlement moves the funds. The reservation prevents double-spending by reducing available_balance immediately after authorisation. The final ledger debit at settlement may differ from the authorisation amount (gratuity, currency variance) — using a reservation at auth time and final posting at settlement is the correct accounting treatment under IFRS and Visa/Mastercard rules.
design_decisions.accounting_treatment: Debit: balance reservation account (authorisation); Credit: available_balance. Final settlement: Debit: account ledger; Credit: balance reservation release.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-011 can call SVC-009 (Domestic Payments) directly for settlement funds movement — both are within CAP-003.
design_decisions.rationale: CAP-003.05 (Card Processing, SVC-011) and CAP-003.01 (Faster Payments / Domestic Payments, SVC-009) are sub-capabilities of the same parent capability (CAP-003 Payment Operations). The bank's architectural principle permits direct API calls within the same capability. SVC-011 calls SVC-009 for settlement funds disbursement (BACS/CHAPS) in PH-045. This is the only synchronous call in this journey and it occurs in the batch clearing/settlement phase — well outside the real-time authorisation latency constraint.
